rationale: Greek loanword βαθμός 'step, grade, rank.' Standard ecclesiastical term for graded ranks in the catechumenate/elect hierarchy. Here ⲡⲃⲁⲑⲙⲟⲥ ⲛ̄ⲧⲙⲛⲧⲕⲁⲧⲏⲭⲟⲩⲙⲉⲛⲟⲥ = 'the step of the catechumenate,' the foundational grade of initiation.

Lycopolitan ⲍⲙⲁⲧ = ⲥⲙⲟⲧ 'form, kind, manner' with regular ⲍ for ⲥ in onset. Distinct from ⲥⲙⲟⲧ proper. Used here in 'this kind of faith of this manner' — the type of faith characteristic of the catechumen-grade.
Lycopolitan ⲉⲛⲧ⸗ = Sahidic ⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'bring, lead' with object suffix; parallel formation to standard. Confirmed by line 6: ⲟⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲩ 'bring them.'

Standard Manichaean initiation-ritual term: the 'right hand of peace' (dextera pacis) extended to the catechumen, marking his reception into the community. Cf. Galatians 2:9 (NT background). Recurs throughout Manichaean ritual texts.

Substantival use of the qualitative ⲱⲁⲣⲡ 'first' (Lyc. = ϣⲟⲣⲡ̄): 'the first principle, the first stage, the foundation-step.' Here ⲕⲁ ⲧⲱⲁⲣⲡ ⲙ̄ⲡⲗⲁⲛⲏ 'set the firstness/initiation away from error' = take the inaugural step of conversion.

Greek loanword ἀποδημία 'journey from home, going abroad.' Already related to glossary entry ⲁⲡⲟⲍⲏⲙⲓ 'to go on a journey' (verb). Here in noun form: 'the journey-forth of all those works' = their departure from their imprisonment in matter to the Height.
